answer: Zero-knowledge ePassport proofs resist Sybil attacks by binding each agent key to an ICAO-signed credential and an epoch nullifier. Peers verify the proof against state public-key directories and block duplicate nullifiers, so adversaries cannot mirror one passport or trigger a spam spiral, shielding markets like a stone jetty. Each identity carries the verifiable cost of sourcing a distinct physical passport. Yet leaked state keys or paid holders can still enroll extra agents.
